name: Jawe
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Ozanne-Rivierre, F. 1982. Langues du Hienghene et proto-oceanien: phonologie comparee (covers Jawe phonology); not online-accessible

sources.citation: Leblic, Isabelle. 2020. Françoise Ozanne-Rivierre et Jean-Claude Rivierre, deux linguistes engagés auprès des Kanak et de leurs langues. JSO 151: 125-158 (doi 10.4000/jso.12282).
sources.note: direct download summary only (OpenEdition bot wall by automated download): Jawe appears only in lists of Hienghène languages covered by the 1982 dictionary; no Jawe-specific description in the Rivierres' bibliography.

sources.citation: Académie des Langues Kanak, page 'Jawe' and notice of Camoui, Cauchard & Pada 2018 Lexique thématique caac et jawe (ALK, Nouméa).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Speaker numbers and texts only; the 2018 lexique is print-only (not opened).

sources.citation: DGLFLF/LACITO 'Corpus de la parole' fiche 'Jawe' (c. 2008, the Internet Archive 2011).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology; confirms the entire linguistic documentation of Jawe = Haudricourt & Ozanne-Rivierre 1982, Leenhardt 1946 no.18 (pp.117-122), Guillaumin 1941 plant list, unpublished Ozanne-Rivierre texts.

sources.citation: Lynch, Ross & Crowley 2002 The Oceanic Languages; Blust 2013 The Austronesian Languages (on-disk texts).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Jawe sketch in LRC 2002; Blust gives only Jawe inventory size (34 C, 7 V + length + nasal). Nothing on Jawe stress.

sources.citation: Rivierre, Jean-Claude. 1991. Loss of final consonants in the north of New Caledonia. In R. Blust (ed.), Currents in Pacific linguistics, 415-432. Pacific Linguistics C-117.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Jawe appears in abbreviation list and cognate tables only; the only stress remarks concern Cèmuhî ('the last syllable can be equated with an unstressed syllable'; 'in polysyllables, FCs appear in unstressed position'). No Jawe stress rule.

sources.citation: Rivierre, Jean-Claude. 1978. Accents, tons et inversion tonale en Nouvelle-Calédonie. BSLP 73(1): 415-443.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes initial demarcative accent in Xârâcùù (South) and tone in Centre/Far South; Jawe ('jawé') is used only as the source of Nord examples in a consonant-correspondence table (p.429, n.8). No statement on Jawe accent.

sources.citation: Ozanne-Rivierre, Françoise. 1975. La littérature orale nemi (Nouvelle-Calédonie). JSO 31(49): 399-434.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p.402 initial accent — Nemi only; nothing on Jawe.

sources.citation: Rivierre [Ozanne-Rivierre], Françoise. 1975. Phonologie du némi (Nouvelle-Calédonie) et notes sur les consonnes postnasalisées. BSLP 70(1): 345-356.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p.351: 'L'accent se porte généralement sur la première syllabe' — for NEMI (sister language, same Hienghène group), not Jawe; Jawe not treated.

sources.citation: Voegelin, C.F. & F.M. Voegelin. 1964. Languages of the World: Indo-Pacific fascicle three. Anthropological Linguistics 6(9) (ERIC ED010354).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists 'Jawe (Ubach), 400 speakers' under Nemi; no stress information for Jawe.

sources.citation: Haudricourt, A.-G. 1961. Richesse en phonèmes et richesse en locuteurs. L'Homme 1(1): 5-10.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: General remarks on NC phoneme inventories and prosodic levelling; nothing on Jawe accent.

sources.citation: Leenhardt, Maurice. 1946. Langues et dialectes de l'Austro-Mélanésie. Travaux et Mémoires de l'Institut d'Ethnologie 46. Paris: Institut d'Ethnologie. Ch. 18 'Jawe' pp. 117-121 and general 'Phonétique' pp. 4-11 (Gallica ark:/12148/bpt6k21694f, open images; scanned run here).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent: p.117 §1 gives a Jawe consonant/vowel transcription table, §2 'Accent et ton' is printed as a bare heading with nothing under it; the general chapter (p.11) says 'Il reste à connaître l'accent, le ton.. On en trouvera le détail au chapitre réservé à chacune de celles-ci' — and the Jawe chapter leaves it blank.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Consonant-history tables (after Ozanne-Rivierre 1992/1995); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Haudricourt, A.-G., J.-C. Rivierre, F. Rivierre, C. Moyse-Faurie & J. de La Fontinelle. 1979. Les langues mélanésiennes de Nouvelle-Calédonie. Collection Eveil 13. Nouméa: D.E.C., Bureau psychopédagogique.

sources.note: Pedagogical overview with short notices per language/region (F. Rivierre on the Hienghène languages); may give a one-line accent statement for the Hienghène group including Jawe.

sources.citation: Ozanne-Rivierre, Françoise & Jean-Claude Rivierre. 2004. Évolution des formes canoniques dans les langues de Nouvelle-Calédonie. Faits de Langues 23-24 (Les langues austronésiennes, E. Zeitoun dir.): 141-153.

sources.note: Pan-New-Caledonian account of canonical word shapes and prosody by the two fieldworkers; probable locus of a North (initial accent) vs Centre/South typology covering Jawe.

sources.citation: Ozanne-Rivierre, Françoise. 1995. Structural changes in the languages of Northern New Caledonia. Oceanic Linguistics 34(1): 45-72.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: First-hand comparative phonology of the Northern languages incl. Jawe (aspirates from reduplication under stress); most likely place for an explicit statement that Northern NC languages (Jawe included) have word-initial stress.

sources.citation: Rivierre, Jean-Claude. 1993. Tonogenesis in New Caledonia. In J.A. Edmondson & K.J. Gregerson (eds), Tonality in Austronesian languages, 155-173. Oceanic Linguistics Special Publication 24. Honolulu: U. Hawaii Press.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: online with a university library login
sources.note: Explains Centre tones vs North aspirates from an earlier initial stress accent; likely contains an explicit synchronic statement about stress in the (non-tonal) Northern languages such as Jawe.

sources.citation: Haudricourt, A.-G. & F. Ozanne-Rivierre. 1982. Dictionnaire thématique des langues de la région de Hienghène (Nouvelle-Calédonie): pije, fwâi, nemi, jawe, précédé d'une Phonologie comparée des langues de Hienghène et du proto-océanien (pp. 9-61) + per-language phonological presentations (c. pp. 62-70). LACITO-documents Asie-Austronésie 4. Paris: SELAF. 285 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only modern first-hand description covering Jawe phonology (Ozanne-Rivierre's own fieldwork, informant Félix Kawa of Yambé); the Jawe sound-system presentation is where an accent statement would sit. IA full-text snippets suggest it may be silent on accent, but scanned-based search is not proof — needs eyes on the printed pages.

sources.citation: Ozanne-Rivierre, Françoise (1982). Langues du Hienghène et proto-océanien: phonologie comparée. In Dictionnaire Thématique des Langues de la région de Hienghène (Nouvelle-Calédonie): Pije - Fwâi - Nemi - Jawe. Louvain: Peeters. pp. 9-61.
